rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques are God's houses on earth, illuminating the people of heaven as stars illuminate the people of earth.
rows.anchor: المساجد بيوت الله في الأرض وهي تضيء لأهل السماء كما تضيء النجوم لأهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies the houses as four mosques built by prophets: the Kaaba, Jerusalem, Medina, and Quba.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها أربع مساجد لم يبنها إلا نبي الكعبة بناها إبراهيم وإسماعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as the houses of prophets and, by extension, the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي بيوت الأنبياء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked which houses the verse meant, the Prophet said prophets' houses; he affirmed that Ali and Fatima's house was among the most excellent.
rows.anchor: أنه سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قرأ الآية أي بيوت هذه فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi supports the household interpretation with the purification verse and the greeting to the People of the House.
rows.anchor: وقوله ورحمة الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's permission concerns raising the houses of prophets and successors; raising means honoring them, elevating their rank, and purifying them from sins and impurities.
rows.anchor: فالإذن يرفع بيوت الأنبياء والأوصياء مطلق والمراد بالرفع التعظيم ورفع القدر من الأرجاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes raising the houses to mean bringing one's needs before God in them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد برفعها رفع الحوائج فيها إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mentioning God's name in the houses means reciting His Book there.
rows.anchor: أي يتلى فيها كتابه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that God's most beautiful names are mentioned in the houses.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تذكر فيها أسماؤه الحسنى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: The morning and evening glorification means performing prayer at dawn and in the evenings.
rows.anchor: أي يصلى له فيها بالبكور والعشايا عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says every occurrence of tasbih in the Quran means prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كل تسبيح في القرآن صلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines tasbih as declaring God free of what cannot be attributed to Him and affirming the fitting attributes of His wise acts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالتسبيح تنزيه الله تعالى عما لا يجوز عليه

words: رِجَالٌۭ لَّا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَٰرَةٌۭ وَلَا بَيْعٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The men are not occupied or diverted by trade or sale from remembering God and establishing prayer.
rows.anchor: أي لا تشغلهم ولا تصرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In iqām al-ṣalāh, the feminine ending is omitted because it replaces the wāw in aqwām; annexation supplies the ending's role.
rows.anchor: أي إقامة الصلاة حذف الهاء لأنها عوض عن الواو

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: They are people who leave trade and go to prayer when its time arrives, earning more than those who continue trading.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر ع وأبي عبد الله ع أنهم قوم إذا حضرت الصلاة تركوا التجارة وانطلقوا إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains giving alms as sincere obedience to God.
rows.anchor: أي إخلاص الطاعة لله تعالى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan takes the phrase to mean the obligatory alms-tax.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يريد الزكاة المفروضة عن الحسن

words: يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًۭا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ
rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: The day is the Resurrection, when hearts and eyes pass through changing states as the Fire scorches, roasts, and burns them.
rows.anchor: أراد يوم القيامة تتقلب فيه أحوال القلوب والأبصار وتنتقل من حال إلى حال فتلفحها النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says hearts swing between hope of rescue and fear of ruin, while eyes look right and left to learn where books and people will be taken.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب فيه القلوب بين الطمع في النجاة والخوف من الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says hearts rise to the throats and sight becomes blindness after seeing.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تتقلب القلوب ببلوغها الحناجر والأبصار بالعمى بعد البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the change as hearts moving from doubt to faith and eyes seeing guidance where they formerly saw error; the insightful gain further insight.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه تنتقل القلوب عن الشك إلى اليقين والإيمان

rows.speaker: مسلم بن محارب
rows.claim: In a noncanonical reading, Muslim ibn Muḥārib reads fadamrān-hum with the emphatic nūn; it is also related from Ali as a dual command to Moses and Aaron to destroy them.
rows.anchor: قراءة مسلم بن محارب فدمرانهم تدميرا على التأكيد بالنون الثقيلة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ali has fadamrāhum, understood as a command to Moses and Aaron to destroy them.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن علي ع وعنه فدمراهم وهذا كأنه أمر لموسى وهارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An enemy is one who keeps distant from helping out of hatred; the root denotes stepping away, and transgression is going far from right.
rows.anchor: العدو المتباعد عن النصرة للبغضة من عدا يعدو إذا باعد خطوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartīl is clear explanation delivered calmly and successively.
rows.anchor: والترتيل التبيين في تثبيت وترسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tooth described as ratl or ratil is spaced and has no crowding or gaps.
rows.anchor: وثغر رتل ورتل بفتح التاء وسكونها إذا كان مفلجا لا لصص فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadmīr means destruction, with the sense of a striking or extraordinary calamity; the verb can mean attacking someone with harm.
rows.anchor: فالتدمير الإهلاك لأمر عجيب ومنه التنكيل يقال دمر على فلان إذا هجم عليه بالمكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rass is a well that has not been lined with stones or other material.
rows.anchor: والرس البئر التي لم تطو بحجارة ولا غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabbīr means destruction; its noun is tabār, and tibr denotes broken pieces of gold.
rows.anchor: والتتبير الإهلاك والاسم منه التبار ومنه قيل التبر لقطع الذهب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj allows hādiyan wa-naṣīran as either circumstantial accusatives or a specification of the sufficiency expressed by the verb.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: { هاديا ونصيرا } منصوب على وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jumlatan is accusative as a circumstantial expression meaning all together; aḥsana is genitive, coordinated with al-ḥaqq.
rows.anchor: جملة نصب على الحال معناه مجموعا وأحسن مجرور بالعطف على الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase on their faces is a circumstantial accusative, meaning they are gathered face-down.
rows.anchor: { على وجوههم } في موضع نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawm Nūḥ is accusative under an implied verb, estimated as We drowned the people of Noah.
rows.anchor: وقوم نوح منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره هذا الظاهر تقديره أغرقنا قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb aghraqnāhum governs the temporal phrase lammā.
rows.anchor: والعامل في لما أغرقناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀd and Thamūd may coordinate with the pronoun in jaʿalnāhum, or with the meaning of the prior promise of punishment.
rows.anchor: وعادا وثمود وما بعد ذلك عطف على الهاء والميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullan is accusative under an omitted verb explained by the verb that follows.
rows.anchor: وكلا منصوب بفعل مضمر الذي ظهر تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṭar al-sūʾ is accusative as a verbal noun, estimated as imṭār al-sūʾ.
rows.anchor: منصوب لأنه مصدر أمطرت تقديره إمطار السوء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: As God made Muhammad enemies among his people, He made every prophet enemies among the disbelievers of their own people.
rows.anchor: وكما جعلنا لك عدوا من مشركي قومك جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من كفار قومه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to call people to faith, abandon ancestral religion and idol worship, and condemn idols gave them cause to oppose the prophets.
rows.anchor: أمر الأنبياء ع أن يدعوهم إلى الإيمان بالله تعالى وترك ما ألفوه من دينهم ودين آبائهم وإلى ترك عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God suffices as guide to truth and as helper for His allies against their enemies in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: حسبك بالله هاديا إلى الحق وناصرا لأوليائه في الدنيا والآخرة على أعدائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says God guides prophets to avoid criminals' hostility by seeking refuge in Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هاديا للأنبياء إلى التحرز عن عداوة المجرمين

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers asked why the Quran was not delivered to Muhammad all at once, as they said the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms had been.
rows.anchor: هلا أتيتنا بالقرآن جملة واحدة كما أنزلت التوراة والإنجيل والزبور جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent it gradually to strengthen the Prophet's heart: fresh revelation for each event increased his certainty and insight.
rows.anchor: أي لنقوي به قلبك فتزداد بصيرة

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that earlier books came down written because their prophets could read and write, whereas the unlettered Prophet received the Quran in installments.
rows.anchor: لأنها نزلت على الأنبياء يكتبون ويقرؤون فنزلت عليهم مكتوبة والقرآن إنما نزل على نبي أمي لا يكتب ولا يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual revelation also fits the Quran's abrogating and abrogated rulings, answers to questions, corrections of events, and reports of happenings.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فإن في القرآن الناسخ والمنسوخ وفيه ما هو جواب لمن سأله عن أمور

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada explain tartīl as clear explanation and sending the revelation successively, one part after another.
rows.anchor: أي بيناه تبيينا وأرسلناه ترسيلا بعضه في أثر بعض عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains the phrase as setting the Quran out distinctly.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فصلناه تفصيلا عن السدي

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī explains it as dividing the Quran into parts.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فرقناه تفريقا عن النخعي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ibn Abbas to recite clearly, not scatter or rush the words like poetry, pause at its marvels, and move hearts rather than merely finish a sūra.
rows.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about night as a time of repose is linked to the statement that God made night so people could rest.
rows.anchor: لتسكنوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subāt means rest for bodies and a cessation of work.
rows.anchor: أي راحة لأبدانكم وقطعا لأعمالكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines subāt as stopping movement while the spirit remains in the body.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: السبات أن ينقطع عن الحركة والروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day is nushūr because the spirit spreads through the body upon waking; the term also recalls resurrection.
rows.anchor: لانتشار الروح باليقظة فيه مأخوذ من نشور البعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another explanation takes nushūr as people dispersing by day to seek their needs and livelihoods.
rows.anchor: لأن الناس ينتشرون فيه لطلب حوائجهم ومعايشهم فيكون النشور هنا بمعنى التفرق لابتغاء الرزق عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi refers readers to his earlier discussion of the wind sent ahead of God's mercy in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: مضى الكلام فيه في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is pure in itself and purifies others by removing ritual impurities and filth.
rows.anchor: أي طاهرا في نفسه ومطهرا لغيره مزيلا للأحداث والنجاسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead town is a barren place without growth; town is masculine here because it can mean a district or place.
rows.anchor: قد مات بالجدب وأراد بالبلدة البلد أو المكان فلذلك قال ميتا بالتذكير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The rain brings out plants and fruits.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لنخرج به النبات والثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is given to numerous livestock, or made a source of drinking water for livestock.
rows.anchor: أي ولنسقي من ذلك الماء أنعاما جمة أو نجعله سقيا لأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anāsī means many people.
rows.anchor: أي أناسا كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain is circulated among the regions of the earth; alternatively, it is apportioned so no place receives too much or too little, with variation according to benefit.
rows.anchor: أي صرفنا المطر بينهم يدور في جهات الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should reflect on the rain as evidence of God's power and that no one else deserves worship.
rows.anchor: أي ليتفكروا ويستدلوا به على سعة مقدورنا ولأنه لا يستحق العبادة غيرنا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ingratitude includes claiming that rain came because of a particular star.
rows.anchor: فيقولون مطرنا بنوء كذا وكذا عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view understands the people's denial as rejection of resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فأبوا إلا كفورا بالبعث والنشور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hijaz readers, Abu Amr, Hafs, and Zayd read nuzila lightly with al-rūḥ al-amīn nominative; the other readers geminate the verb and put the Spirit in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز وأبو عمرو وحفص وزيد نزل بالتخفيف الروح الأمين بالرفع والباقون نزل بالتشديد الروح الأمين بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads the verb with feminine tāʾ and āya in the nominative; the other readers use masculine yāʾ and put āya in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر أو لم تكن بالتاء آية بالرفع والباقون لم يكن بالياء آية بالنصب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Among the anomalous readings, al-Hasan has al-aʿjamiyyīn, feminine taʾ in fa-taʾtīhim, and al-shayāṭūn.
rows.anchor: في الشواذ قراءة الحسن والأعجميين وقراءته أيضا فتأتيهم بغتة بالتاء ما تنزلت به الشياطون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali supports geminated nazzala with other Quranic uses of the verb; with the ungeminated reading, God sends the Spirit by His command, yielding the same sense.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: حجة من قال نزل به بالتشديد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains feminine takun by an implicit story pronoun interpreted by the following clause; alternatively, the clause أن يعلمه itself is the feminine āya in meaning.
rows.anchor: والوجه في قراءة ابن عامر أو لم تكن لهم آية إن في تكن ضمير القصة والحديث

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says al-aʿjamiyyīn explains canonical baʿḍ al-aʿjamīn: the relative yāʾ is dropped and the masculine plural signals it, despite the usual adjective pattern.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جني: في قراءة الحسن الأعجميين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine verb fa-taʾtīhim has al-sāʿa, the Hour, omitted as its subject, signaled by the punishment that occurs then and frequent Quranic references to its coming.
rows.anchor: فتأتيهم بغتة بالتاء معناه فتأتيهم الساعة فأضمر الساعة لدلالة العذاب الواقع فيها عليها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra calls al-Hasan's form al-shayāṭūn a mistake.
rows.anchor: فقد قال الفراء فيه: غلط الشيخ يعني الحسن

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Nadr objects that if poetry by al-Aʿjāj and Ruʾba can be cited, al-Hasan's reading should be accepted too, especially since he must have heard it.
rows.anchor: فقيل ذلك للنضر بن شميل فقال إذا جاز أن يحتج بقول العجاج ورؤبة

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says even eloquent speakers can confuse similar plurals; shayāṭūn is an error but resembles forms such as masīl/muslān and maʿīn/maʿnān.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني: هذا مما يعرض مثله للفصيح لتداخل الجمعين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the reader analogized the ending to Yabrīn and Filasṭīn, where Arabs vary whether inflection falls on nūn or the preceding letter; he derives it from ruin.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الوجه فيه أنه رأى آخره كآخر يبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿjam is one whose tongue resists Arabic; ʿajamī is the opposite of Arab, while aʿjamī is the opposite of eloquent.
rows.anchor: اللغة: الأعجم الذي يمتنع لسانه عن العربية والعجمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā yuʾminūna bihi is a circumstantial accusative, and baghtatan is a verbal noun used as a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمنون به في موضع النصب على الحال وبغتة مصدر وضع موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinīn functions as a time adverb modifying the period of enjoyment.
rows.anchor: سنين ظرف زمان لمتعناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in mā aghnā is negative, and aghnā has an omitted object meaning their enjoyment benefited them nothing.
rows.anchor: ما أغنى ما نافية ومفعول أغنى محذوف وتقديره ما أغنى عنهم تمتعهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikrā is accusative as an expression of purpose.
rows.anchor: ذكرى في محل النصب لأنه مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mā yanbaghī, the hidden subject refers back to the act of descent: it is not fitting for them to bring it down.
rows.anchor: وما ينبغي فاعل ينبغي مستكن فيه عائد إلى مصدر تنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting earlier prophets, the commentary turns to the Quran to connect their accounts with the story of Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ثم بين سبحانه أمر القرآن بعد أن قص أخبار الأنبياء ع ليتصل بها حديث نبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is revelation from the Lord of the worlds, brought down by the trustworthy Spirit, Gabriel, who does not change or alter it.
rows.anchor: أي نزل الله بالقرآن { الروح الأمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is called Spirit because he revives religion; another view says he revives souls through blessings, and another that he is a spiritual body.
rows.anchor: وسماه روحا لأنه يحيي به الدين. وقيل: لأنه يحيي به الأرواح بما ينزل من البركات. وقيل: لأنه جسم روحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descent on Muhammad's heart is figurative: God makes Gabriel hear and memorize the revelation, then Gabriel recites it for the Prophet to retain by heart.
rows.anchor: وهذا على سبيل التوسع لأن الله تعالى يسمعه جبرائيل ع فيحفظه وينزل به على الرسول ويقرأه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran equips Muhammad to warn people through God's signs.
rows.anchor: أي لتخوف به الناس وتنذرهم بآيات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic is a clear language that explains what people need for their religion.
rows.anchor: أي بلغة العرب مبين للناس ما بهم إليه الحاجة في دينهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means Quraysh's dialect, so they would understand it rather than claim not to understand Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به لسان قريش ليفهموا ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the language as that of Jurhum; it is Arabic because the Prophet and audience were Arabs and its eloquence challenged Arab masters, honoring Arabic as the language of Paradise's people.
rows.anchor: وقيل لسان جرهم وإنما جعله عربيا لأن المنزل عليه عربي والمخاطبون به عرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran and news of Muhammad appear in earlier scriptures as glad tidings; this does not mean God revealed the Quran to anyone besides Muhammad. Zubur is plural of zabūr.
rows.anchor: أي في كتب الأولين على وجه البشارة به وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لا بمعنى أن الله أنزله على غير محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says earlier prophets taught the same call to monotheism, justice, and resurrection, and related accounts of nations.
rows.anchor: وقيل. معناه أنه أنزل على سائر الأنبياء من الدعاء إلى التوحيد والعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelite scholars' knowledge that the Quran's coming had been foretold in their scriptures is evidence for Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: معناه أولم يكن لهم علم علماء بني إسرائيل بمجيئه على ما تقدمت البشارة دلالة لهم على صحة نبوته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Israelite scholars as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions; their reports helped convert the Aws and Khazraj.
rows.anchor: وعلماء بني إسرائيل عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israelites told Arabs of the Quran's mention in their books and foretold the Prophet, which contributed to the conversion of Aws and Khazraj.
rows.anchor: وكانت اليهود تبشر به وتستفتح على العرب به وكان ذلك سبب إسلام الأوس والخزرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading of allā yāsjudū is construed as an address with an omitted vocative such as qawm; the supplied poetry illustrates this deletion.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ما حكي عن أبي عمرو من قوله يا ويل له ويجوز أن يراد بعد يا مأمورون فحذفوا

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd's verse about being told ya-smaʿ illustrates an omitted person addressed after yā.
rows.anchor: فمن تلك ما أنشده أبو زيد:

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's greeting to the dwelling of May provides another poetic example of the vocative construction.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الزجاج لذي الرمة:

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal's greeting to Hind is cited as a further poetic example of the same vocative pattern.
rows.anchor: وللأخطل: ألا يا اسلمي يا هند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mushaf's written yāʾ supports the geminated reading allā yasjudū; the light reading would instead have the imperative asjudū without yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ومما يؤكد قراءة من قرأ ألا يسجدوا بالتشديد أنها لو كانت مخففة لما كانت في يسجدوا ياء لأنها اسجدوا

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Readers use third-person yukhfūn/yʿlinūn because the discourse is in third person; al-Kisaʾi uses second-person forms as the discourse shifts to address on asjudū.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ يخفون ويعلنون بالياء فلأن الكلام على الغيبة وقراءة الكسائي فيهما بالتاء لأن الكلام قد دخله خطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant allā yā asjudū can address both believers and disbelievers previously mentioned in the third person.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ ألا يا اسجدوا فيجوز أن يكون الخطاب للمؤمنين والكافرين الذين جرى ذكرهم على لفظ الغيبة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr keeps the yāʾ in māli silent here but opens it in the phrase at 36:22, avoiding a pause between māli and the following negation.
rows.anchor: كان أبو عمرو يسكن الياء في قوله { مالي لا أرى الهدهد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā arā is a circumstantial accusative construction.
rows.anchor: ولا أرى في موضع نصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is a disconnected interrogative meaning rather, is he among the absent? Kāna has the sense of yakūnu.
rows.anchor: أم منقطعة التقدير بل أهو من الغائبين وكان بمعنى يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām answers an implicit oath.
rows.anchor: واللام في لأعذبنه جواب قسم مقدر أي والله لأعذبنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayra baʿīd modifies an omitted verbal noun, meaning a short period of waiting.
rows.anchor: غير بعيد منصوب لأنه صفة مصدر تقديره فمكث وقتا غير بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yasjudūn is a circumstantial clause dependent on wajadtu.
rows.anchor: ويسجدون في موضع نصب على الحال من وجدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman checked on the birds and looked for the hoopoe when he noticed it was missing.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر سبحانه عن سليمان فقال { وتفقد الطير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā lī lā arā means why do I not see the hoopoe; the expression is an Arabic reversal like mā lī arāka kaʾīban, meaning what is wrong with you.
rows.anchor: أي ما للهدهد لا أراه تقول العرب مالي أراك كئيبا ومعناه مالك ولكنه من القلب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Sulayman needed the hoopoe on a journey to locate underground water, which it could see as one sees oil in a bottle.
rows.anchor: لأنه يقال أنه يرى الماء في بطن الأرض كما يراه في القارورة عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: In an exchange with Abu Hanifa, Abu Abd Allah says the hoopoe detects underground water; Abu Hanifa jokes that it still failed to see the trap, and Abu Abd Allah replies that fate blinds sight.
rows.anchor: قال قال أبو حنيفة لأبي عبد الله ع: كيف تفقد سليمان الهدهد من بين الطير

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Sulayman checked for the hoopoe because it had failed to attend its assigned watch.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما تفقده لإخلاله بنوبته عن وهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the birds shaded Sulayman from the sun, so the missing hoopoe became apparent when sunlight fell on him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت الطيور تظله من الشمس فلما أخل الهدهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman asks whether the hoopoe is delayed in disobedience or absent for an excuse or need.
rows.anchor: معناه أتأخر عصيانا أم غاب لعذر وحاجة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says Sulayman first assumed the hoopoe was present but unseen, then shifted to asking whether it was actually absent.
rows.anchor: لما تفقد سليمان الطير ولم ير الهدهد قال ما لي لا أرى الهدهد على تقدير أنه مع جنوده وهو لا يراه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: A severe punishment would mean plucking the hoopoe's feathers and leaving it in the sun.
rows.anchor: معناه لأعذبنه بنتف ريشه وإلقائه في الشمس عن ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that Sulayman would put it among its enemies or antagonists.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بأن أجعله بين أضداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because birds' speech and legal responsibility in Sulayman's time were his miracle, the hoopoe could be reproached and punished for disobeying him.
rows.anchor: وكما صح نطق الطير وتكليفه في زمانه معجزة له جازت معاتبته على ما وقع منه من تقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative threat is to cut the hoopoe's throat as punishment for disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي لأقطعن حلقه عقوبة على عصيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoopoe could escape punishment by presenting a clear proof that excuses its absence.
rows.anchor: أي بحجة واضحة تكون له عذرا في الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says Sulayman waited only a short time; another says the hoopoe was away briefly and returned, possibly staying in a nearby place.
rows.anchor: أي فلم يلبث سليمان إلا زمانا يسيرا حتى جاء الهدهد.

words: فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the hoopoe returned with a proof and knowledge Sulayman and his troops did not have, including news unknown to human beings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فأتاه الهدهد بحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode shows that someone living in a prophet's time may know something the prophet does not know.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه يجوز أن يكون في زمن الأنبياء من يعرف ما لا يعرفونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḥāṭa means knowing a thing from every side on which it can be known, likened to a wall enclosing what is inside.
rows.anchor: وعلم الإحاطة وهو أن يعلم الشيء من جميع جهاته التي يمكن أن يعلم عليها تشبيها بالسور المحيط بما فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies Sabaʾ as a city in Yemen.
rows.anchor: وسبأ مدينة بأرض اليمن عن قتادة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says God sent twelve prophets to Sabaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى بعث إلى سبأ إثني عشر نبيا عن السدي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Asked about Sabaʾ, the Prophet described a man with ten Arab sons: six tribes settled in the south and four in the north, naming their descendants.
rows.anchor: وروى علقمة بن وعلة عن ابن عباس قال سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman rules the people so completely that no one challenges her authority; she has every kind of wealth and royal adornment.
rows.anchor: أي تتصرف فيهم بحيث لا يعترض عليها أحد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the woman as Bilqis, daughter of Sharāḥīl and queen of Sabaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: وهي بلقيس بنت شراحيل ملكة سبأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another genealogy says Sharhabil begot her and forty kings, with her father Sharhabil the last of them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: شرحبيل ولدها أربعون ملكا آخرهم أبوها شرحبيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says her council consisted of 312 chiefs, each commanding a thousand fighters.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: وكان أولو مشورتها ثلاثمائة واثني عشر قيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her throne exceeded Sulayman's: its front was gold inlaid with ruby and emerald, its rear silver with jewels, and it had seven locked chambers.
rows.anchor: أي سرير أعظم من سريرك وكان مقدمه من ذهب مرصع بالياقوت الأحمر والزمرد الأخضر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas measures Bilqis's throne as thirty cubits long and wide and thirty cubits high.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال كان عرش بلقيس ثلاثين ذراعا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim interprets the throne as sovereignty.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: المراد بالعرش الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilqis and her people worship the sun instead of God; Satan beautifies this worship, blocks them from the true path, and they are not guided.
rows.anchor: وجدتها وقومها يسجدون للشمس من دون الله وزين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saddahum means Satan turned them away from the path of truth.
rows.anchor: أي صرفهم عن سبيل الحق

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues the hoopoe did not know God, but inferred that worship contrary to Sulayman's practice was false, like a child observing worshippers.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: لم يكن الهدهد عارفا بالله تعالى وإنما أخبر بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi rejects al-Jubbāʾī: distinguishing worship of God from sun worship as right and wrong requires knowledge of God, and attributing misguidance to Satan implies knowledge of divine justice.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره خلاف ظاهر القرآن لأنه لا يجوز أن يفرق بين الحق الذي هو السجود لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With lightening, allā yāsjudū can command prostration, with a warning yāʾ or an omitted qawm; it may also be a divine command interjected into the account or the hoopoe's protest to Sabaʾ or Sulayman.
rows.anchor: قد بينا أن التخفيف إنما هو على معنى الأمر بالسجود ودخلت الياء للتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The geminated reading means Satan made their misguidance attractive so that they would not prostrate to God.
rows.anchor: والقراءة بالتشديد على معنى زين لهم الشيطان ضلالتهم لئلا يسجدوا لله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the geminated reading does not require a prostration of recitation.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء إن القراءة بالتشديد لا توجب سجدة التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabrisi rejects al-Farra: the wording reproaches them for leaving prostration and therefore indicates that prostration is obligatory, as in 25:60.
rows.anchor: وهذا غير صحيح لأن الكلام قد تضمن الذم على ترك السجود فيه دلالة على وجوب السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khabʾ is something hidden behind a barrier that prevents detection; the verbal noun is used adjectivally, and what God creates from nothing is like a hidden thing brought out.
rows.anchor: الخبء المخبوء وهو ما أحاط به غيره حتى منع من إدراكه وهو مصدر وصف به

rows.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid take khabʾ as the unseen: everything hidden from perception in the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الخبء الغيب وهو كل ما غاب عن الإدراك فالمعنى يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض عن عكرمة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies heaven's hidden thing as rain and earth's as plants and trees.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أن خبء السماوات المطر وخبء الأرض النبات والأشجار عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people conceal and reveal means what is secret and public.
rows.anchor: أي يعلم السر والعلانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement through Lord of the great throne may finish the hoopoe's speech or begin God's own report.
rows.anchor: إلى ههنا تمام الحكاية لما قاله الهدهد ويحتمل أن يكون ابتداء إخبار من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is the royal seat God elevated above the seven heavens; angels surround it and lift servants' deeds toward it, while blessings originate from it, making it the greatest created thing.
rows.anchor: والعرش: سرير الملك الذي عظمه الله ورفعه فوق السماوات السبع وجعل الملائكة تحف به
